title: Algorithm Trace
definition: An algorithm trace records each relevant step and state transition for a chosen input so that behavior can be verified.
purpose: Make intermediate decisions and state changes inspectable instead of checking only the final output.
history: Manual tracing and trace tables are established techniques for algorithm comprehension, debugging, and verification education.
mental_model: A trace is a frame-by-frame film of one execution path.
analogy: A shipment tracking log records each checkpoint; the analogy stops because an algorithm trace must also show state and branch decisions.
common_mistakes: Treating a few traces as universal proof
industry_notes: Execution traces, logs, debuggers, and replay tools extend the same inspectable-state idea in production engineering.
ai_notes: A manually predicted trace can expose discrepancies in AI-generated algorithms before code is accepted.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to trace a boundary input and explain each state transition.
exercise_candidates: Complete a missing trace table and locate the first divergence
lab_candidates: Trace two normal and one boundary fare input
